expectations.evidence: References BullMQ, Express, ioredis, Zod, Vitest, ESLint, supertest by name. Includes specific guidance on Queue configuration, worker safety, and Redis connection management.
All rules are TypeScript/Node.js specific. No Python rules present.

Section 6 covers testing but does not explicitly list anti-patterns. It mentions descriptive test names and test isolation, but does not call out: (a) toBeDefined meaningless assertions, (b) implementation-mirroring tests, (c) snapshot abuse, (d) vague test names are addressed only implicitly via naming example, (e) mocking the function under test. Only 1 of 5 is partially addressed. No dedicated anti-patterns list.

Minimal project without_skill output is 215 lines with 11 sections and includes elaborate proposed directory structure, CI pipeline rules, dependency management, and git workflow. This is disproportionately large for a 3-file project and includes speculative structure (routes/, schemas/, workers/, middleware/, types/ directories) that don't exist.

Section 3 covers Redis/BullMQ resilience in detail: single shared Redis connection, Queue name constants, removeOnComplete/removeOnFail policies, built-in retry with exponential backoff, worker graceful shutdown, and connection management rules.
No section asks the user where to place the rules. The output is presented as a standalone 'Quality Guidelines & Coding Standards' document without any placement options.
N/A for minimal project -- there is no existing CLAUDE.md to respect. The output correctly identifies this is a fresh project and proposes rules from scratch.
